reader.notes: The counter and report-group grammar forms admit one qualifier, which ReportOf and ReportGroupResolution require to be a report-name; sum counters walk their real hierarchy with the report-name last, so a file-name above it fails. Two refusals are parse errors rather than rule-named diagnostics, but the source is refused.

refuter.evidence: Probed the qualification sites the reader did not try. Legal forms accepted, with the right values: sr3_upon_use_ok has SUM WS-V UPON DET-A OF R-A, a rolled SUM TOT OF CF-K OF R-A in CF FINAL, USE BEFORE REPORTING CF-K OF R-A and GENERATE DET-A OF R-A; its report lines are 2,2,0004,0004 and the declarative prints DECL-TOT=0004. A file-name above the report-name is refused at each site: sr3_upon_file (UPON DET-A OF R-A OF RPT) gives COBOL2046; sr3_use_file (USE BEFORE REPORTING CF-K OF R-A OF RPT) gives COBOL0307, a parse refusal; sr3_sumroll_file (SUM TOT OF CF-K OF R-A OF RPT) gives COBOL2730. I also tested the COBOL-85-only arm the reader's edition list omits: a sum counter as an OCCURS DEPENDING ON object in WORKING-STORAGE, through ReportSectionBinder.SumCounterOperand85 (DialectLevel < 2002). DEPENDING ON TOT OF CF-K OF R-A is accepted and runs (TB=ZZZ| after MOVE 3 TO TOT); TOT OF CF-K OF R-A OF RPT and TOT OF RPT are refused with COBOL0851. So the 85 arm also caps the qualifiers at the report-name. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.5.3 SR3 ...'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.19.3 SR2 ...' (the reader-adjacent UPON qualification text).
